subject: Chemistry
description: p-block elements (Groups 13-18): general trends, key compounds, uses

questions.stem: The p-BLOCK in the periodic table consists of which groups?
questions.explanation: p-BLOCK = elements where the LAST valence electron enters a p-orbital. Includes GROUPS 13-18: 13 (Boron family — B, Al, Ga, In, Tl); 14 (Carbon family — C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb); 15 (Nitrogen family — N, P, As, Sb, Bi); 16 (Oxygen family — O, S, Se, Te, Po); 17 (Halogens — F, Cl, Br, I, At); 18 (Noble gases — He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn). Distractor 1 = s-block. Distractor 3 = d-block. Distractor 4 = f-block.

questions.stem: ALUMINIUM (Al, Group 13) is the most abundant METAL in:
questions.explanation: Earth's CRUST composition by mass: O (46%), Si (28%), Al (8.1%), Fe (5%), Ca, Na, K, Mg... ALUMINIUM = MOST ABUNDANT METAL in crust (3rd most abundant element overall). Main ore: BAUXITE (Al₂O₃·xH₂O). India's bauxite: Odisha, Andhra, Jharkhand, Maharashtra. NALCO (Odisha), HINDALCO (UP/Odisha) — major producers. Aluminium uses: aircraft, vehicles, foil, cans, electrical wires, frames. Iron is the most abundant metal in the WHOLE Earth (concentrated in core).

questions.stem: DIAMOND and GRAPHITE are both forms (allotropes) of:
questions.explanation: DIAMOND + GRAPHITE = both pure CARBON, but different structures. DIAMOND: tetrahedral, sp³ hybridised, 3D network → very hard, insulator, refracts light (sparkle). GRAPHITE: layered planar, sp² hybridised, hexagonal sheets → soft, slippery, conducts electricity (free electrons in delocalised π bonds). Other carbon allotropes: FULLERENE (C₆₀ buckyball), GRAPHENE (single layer of graphite — Nobel 2010, Geim + Novoselov), CARBON NANOTUBES, AMORPHOUS (charcoal, soot, coal). DIAMOND + GRAPHITE under STP — graphite slightly more stable.

questions.stem: The most ELECTRONEGATIVE element of the periodic table is:
questions.explanation: FLUORINE (F) — most electronegative element (Pauling scale = 3.98). Top of HALOGENS (Group 17). Strongest oxidiser; readily forms F⁻. EN trend: increases LEFT → RIGHT (across period); DECREASES TOP → BOTTOM (down a group). Top 4 EN: F (3.98), O (3.44), Cl (3.16), N (3.04). Cesium / Francium least EN. F is so reactive it reacts with most things (water, glass) — special handling needed. Used in fluorides (toothpaste), Teflon (PTFE), refrigerants (Freons banned), uranium enrichment (UF₆).

questions.stem: TIN (Sn) and LEAD (Pb), both Group 14 elements, were used historically for making:

options.option_text: Currency coins, only of gold or silver
Steel reinforcement bars used in concrete

questions.explanation: Tin (Sn) + Lead (Pb) — both relatively soft, low-melting metals. Used together: SOLDER (60% Sn / 40% Pb traditional; Pb-free now standard for environment + health) — joins electronic components. PLUMBING — Romans used lead pipes (Latin 'plumbum' = lead, hence symbol Pb + 'plumber'). Lead is TOXIC (neurotoxin); banned from petrol (lead-tetra-ethyl octane booster), paint, pipes. Pb still used in: car batteries, X-ray shields, fishing weights, ammunition. Tin uses: tin cans (steel coated with thin Sn layer), bronze (Cu+Sn), pewter.

questions.stem: INERT pair effect (s-electrons of valence shell unwilling to bond) is most pronounced in which p-block elements?

options.option_text: Top elements of each group only
Heavier ones (Tl, Pb, Bi) at the bottom
Middle elements like Si, As, Se

questions.explanation: INERT PAIR EFFECT — outermost s-electrons (ns² pair) of HEAVIER p-block elements are reluctant to participate in bonding, behaving as 'inert'. Caused by poor shielding by inner d/f electrons → s-electrons held more tightly + farther from valence frontier. Most pronounced for: Tl (Group 13), Pb (Group 14), Bi (Group 15). Result: heavier elements show LOWER OXIDATION STATE more readily than expected. E.g., Pb⁺² (more stable than Pb⁺⁴); Tl⁺ (more stable than Tl⁺³); Bi⁺³ (more stable than Bi⁺⁵). Lighter members (B, C, N) show their group oxidation state more readily.

questions.stem: GLASS (used in windows, bottles) is mainly:

options.option_text: Polymer of plastic with glass colour

questions.explanation: GLASS = AMORPHOUS (non-crystalline) form of SILICA (SiO₂). Made by melting sand (~73% SiO₂), soda ash (Na₂CO₃ ~14%), limestone (CaCO₃ ~9%) at ~1500°C → cools to amorphous solid. Common 'soda-lime glass' for windows, bottles. PYREX = borosilicate (added B₂O₃) — heat-resistant for lab + cookware. CRYSTAL glass = lead glass (PbO added, higher refractive index, 'sparkle'). FIBRE-OPTIC glass = ultra-pure silica with controlled refractive index profile. Glass is technically a SUPERCOOLED LIQUID — flows extremely slowly over long periods.
